title: Why Is It Night? Day, Seasons and the Moon for Kids
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Gizmo the robot, and welcome to Gizmo Explains!
I love asking, how does that work? Today we're going to find out how the sky works.
We'll explore five cool things. Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
When my antenna lights up, it means I have an idea!

lines: Here's a clue: one is bright and sunny, and one is dark and sleepy! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Our Earth is always spinning, like a slow spinning top.
The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night!
Can you spin around slowly, like the Earth? Day, night, day!
How long does one spin take?
Let's say it together: DAY AND NIGHT!
One more time, nice and loud: DAY AND NIGHT!
When it's day for you, it's night for kids on the other side of the world.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: there are four of them: spring, summer, fall, and winter! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Our Earth is tilted, like it's leaning a little to one side.
When your part of Earth leans toward the Sun, it gets more sunshine, and that's summer!
Can you lean to one side, like the tilted Earth?
Earth's tilt as it goes around the Sun!
One more time, nice and loud: SEASONS!
One trip all the way around the Sun takes one whole year.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it can look round, or like a smile in the sky! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
The Moon doesn't make its own light. The Sun shines on it.
As the Moon goes around Earth, we see different parts of its sunny side!
Can you make a round full moon with your arms?
Does the Moon really change shape?
No! We just see more or less of its sunny side.
Let's say it together: MOON PHASES!
One more time, nice and loud: MOON PHASES!
It takes about a month to go from new moon to full moon and back.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: they twinkle in the night sky! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Stars are giant suns, very, very far away.
They're so far away that they look like tiny dots of light!
Can you open and close your hands, like twinkling stars?
Are stars still there in the daytime?
Yes! The Sun is just too bright to see them.
One more time, nice and loud: STARS!
Our Sun is a star too, the closest star to Earth.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's big, bright, and keeps us warm! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
The Sun is a giant ball of hot, glowing gas.
It's so big that one hundred and nine Earths could fit across it, side by side!
Can you stretch your arms out super wide, as big as the Sun?
Why does the Sun look small?
Because it's very, very far away!
Let's say it together: THE SUN!
One more time, nice and loud: THE SUN!
Never look right at the Sun, because it's too bright for your eyes.
Now we know how it works. Great job!

recap: Wow, we learned so much! Let's remember.
Earth spins to make day and night.
We see the Moon's sunny side.
And our Sun is super big!
outro: Which one was your favorite? Keep asking, how does that work?
Bye, friends! See you next time on Gizmo Explains!
